**4.2.2 Internal Recall Investigation Summary — Engineering & Quality**

**Memorandum**
**To:** Managing Director; General Manager, Quality & Regulatory Affairs
**From:** Senior Electrical Engineer, Product Safety
**Date:** 17 July 2026
**Subject:** Root cause investigation — KK7-100 heating element overheat

**Background**
Following the NCSA recall registration on 14 July 2026, the engineering team completed an accelerated root cause investigation using returned units and production records. The investigation is now closed. The summary below is the controlled record of findings.

**Investigation Findings**

1. The heating element assembly (part no. KK7-103, 2000 W rated) uses a mineral-insulated resistance wire element brazed to a stainless steel mounting plate. The brazing process used a lead-free silver solder alloy supplied by our regular vendor.
2. A batch of mounting plates received in February 2025 (supplier lot FEB25-118) had a surface contamination issue. The contamination was identified as residual drawing lubricant not fully removed during the supplier's pre-treatment process.
3. The contaminated plates did not allow proper wetting of the braze alloy. This resulted in incomplete bond lines in approximately 2–4% of assembled elements. The defect was not detected by the standard production resistance test because the elements passed the cold resistance check.
4. Under normal operation, the incomplete bond line creates a higher localised resistance. Over time, this causes localised heating at the junction point. The heating element may overheat in the affected area, leading to elevated kettle body surface temperatures.
5. The boil-dry protection thermostat (KK7-109) operates independently and was not implicated. All units with the defect were manufactured between 3 March 2025 and 15 June 2026.

**Action Items**

The recall was initiated after 11 consumer reports of unusually hot kettle exteriors were received between 1 May 2026 and 30 June 2026. Two reports involved minor skin burns. All affected consumers have been contacted.
- Remove KK7-100 kettles from sale immediately and quarantine stock.
- Display the official recall poster at point of sale (poster supplied by AussieHome).
- Provide customer purchase records to AussieHome within 7 days.
- Process in-store returns and forward returned units to the designated collection centre in Melbourne.

Two retailers requested an extension to the purchase record deadline; this was granted to 31 July.

A public recall notice was published on the AussieHome website and distributed via print media in all states and territories. The notice appeared in major metropolitan newspapers on 6 August and in regional publications on 8 August. The notice was also aired as a short community service announcement on two commercial radio networks in New South Wales and Victoria.

**Executive Summary**

This report documents the conclusion of Recall No. 2026-04, initiated on 16 October 2026, concerning a potential overheating fault in a limited batch of electric kettles manufactured between 22 September and 8 October 2026. The recall was initiated following reports of the kettle base overheating during use, posing a potential burn hazard.

As of 30 November 2026, the recall is closed. The corrective action rate for affected units reached 98.7%, exceeding the target of 95% set by the Product Safety Team. No serious injuries were reported during the recall period. Root cause analysis identified a non-conforming batch of thermal fuses supplied by an external vendor. Corrective actions, including a revised fuse specification and enhanced incoming inspection, have been implemented and verified.

This report provides the regulatory closure documentation, a summary of lessons learned, and details of the prevention plan moving forward.

A component within the kettle's base, specifically the thermal fuse, could fail to operate correctly. This could allow the kettle to overheat, potentially causing the base to become hot to the touch and, in rare cases, melt or emit smoke. No fire or serious injury was reported in Australia.

**4.2.2 Internal Recall Investigation Summary — Engineering & Quality**

**Memorandum**
**To:** Managing Director; General Manager, Quality & Regulatory Affairs
**From:** Senior Electrical Engineer, Product Safety
**Date:** 17 July 2026
**Subject:** Root cause investigation — KK7-100 heating element overheat

**Background**
Following the NCSA recall registration on 14 July 2026, the engineering team completed an accelerated root cause investigation using returned units and production records. The investigation is now closed. The summary below is the controlled record of findings.

**Investigation Findings**

1. The heating element assembly (part no. KK7-103, 2000 W rated) uses a mineral-insulated resistance wire element brazed to a stainless steel mounting plate. The brazing process used a lead-free silver solder alloy supplied by our regular vendor.
2. A batch of mounting plates received in February 2025 (supplier lot FEB25-118) had a surface contamination issue. The contamination was identified as residual drawing lubricant not fully removed during the supplier's pre-treatment process.
3. The contaminated plates did not allow proper wetting of the braze alloy. This resulted in incomplete bond lines in approximately 2–4% of assembled elements. The defect was not detected by the standard production resistance test because the elements passed the cold resistance check.
4. Under normal operation, the incomplete bond line creates a higher localised resistance. Over time, this causes localised heating at the junction point. The heating element may overheat in the affected area, leading to elevated kettle body surface temperatures.
5. The boil-dry protection thermostat (KK7-109) operates independently and was not implicated. All units with the defect were manufactured between 3 March 2025 and 15 June 2026.

**Action Items**

The recall was initiated after 11 consumer reports of unusually hot kettle exteriors were received between 1 May 2026 and 30 June 2026. Two reports involved minor skin burns. All affected consumers have been contacted.

**Prepared by:** M. Chen, Quality Manager
**Approved by:** S. Patel, Managing Director

---

**Executive Summary**

This report documents the conclusion of Recall No. 2026-04, initiated on 16 October 2026, concerning a potential overheating fault in a limited batch of electric kettles manufactured between 22 September and 8 October 2026. The recall was initiated following reports of the kettle base overheating during use, posing a potential burn hazard.

As of 30 November 2026, the recall is closed. The corrective action rate for affected units reached 98.7%, exceeding the target of 95% set by the Product Safety Team. No serious injuries were reported during the recall period. Root cause analysis identified a non-conforming batch of thermal fuses supplied by an external vendor. Corrective actions, including a revised fuse specification and enhanced incoming inspection, have been implemented and verified.

This report provides the regulatory closure documentation, a summary of lessons learned, and details of the prevention plan moving forward.

---

**1. Recall Overview and Chronology**

| Date | Event |
| :--- | :--- |
| 22 Sep – 8 Oct 2026 | Manufacturing period for affected units (Batch K-2609). |
| 14 Oct 2026 | First consumer complaint received regarding overheating base. |
| 16 Oct 2026 | Investigation initiated; affected batch identified. |
| 22 Oct 2026 | Recall No. 2026-04 formally initiated with ACCC notification. |
| 10 Nov 2026 | Customer Care standard response script and email template released. |
| 30 Nov 2026 | End of recall period; corrective action target met. |
| 15 Dec 2026 | Final report issued; recall officially closed. |

**2. Regulatory Closure Documentation**

The following information is provided for the official closure of Recall No. 2026-04 with the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) and the relevant state and territory fair trading offices.

**2.1 Product Information**

- **Product:** AussieHome Electric Kettle, Model KH-2000
- **Colours Affected:** White, Black, and Stainless Steel
- **Batch Identification:** Serial numbers containing the prefix "KH2609" (manufactured between 22 September and 8 October 2026)
- **Number of Units Supplied to Australian Consumers:** 2,450

**2.2 Nature of Defect**

A component within the kettle's base, specifically the thermal fuse, could fail to operate correctly. This could allow the kettle to overheat, potentially causing the base to become hot to the touch and, in rare cases, melt or emit smoke. No fire or serious injury was reported in Australia.

**2.3 Corrective Action Statistics**

| Metric | Value |
| :--- | :--- |
| Total Units Sold | 2,450 |
| Units Returned for Replacement | 1,912 |
| Units Returned for Refund | 505 |
| Units Not Returned (estimated) | 33 |
| **Total Corrective Actions Completed** | **2,417** |
| **Completion Rate** | **98.7%** |

**2.4 Closure Statement**

The recall team confirms that all reasonable efforts have been made to contact affected consumers. The corrective action completion rate of 98.7% has been achieved. The remaining 33 units are presumed to be no longer in use or have been discarded by consumers who did not respond to multiple contact attempts. Given the high completion rate and the absence of reported incidents since the recall was announced, we consider the recall to be complete and formally close this matter as of 30 November 2026.

The sample was submitted by the client for routine product safety and performance verification. Testing was performed in accordance with the following standards, as requested:

- AS/NZS 60335.2.15:2011 (Household electrical appliances – Safety – Particular requirements for appliances for heating liquids)
- AS/NZS 60335.1:2011 (General requirements)
- Internal performance protocol P-31 (heating time, energy consumption, boil-dry protection)

2. SAMPLE DESCRIPTION

| Product name | Kookaburra Electric Kettle |
| Model | KK-900 |

| Rated power | 2200 W |
| Capacity | 1.7 L |
| Construction | Stainless steel body, concealed element, plastic handle/lid |
| Sample condition | New, as received, no visible damage |

3. TEST EQUIPMENT

| Equipment ID | Description | Calibration Due |
|---|---|---|
| EQ-201 | Fluke 289 True RMS Multimeter | 14 Jun 2025 |
| EQ-055 | TTI CPX400DP DC Power Supply (used for reference only) | n/a |
| EQ-119 | Hioki 3334 Power HiTester | 02 Mar 2025 |
| EQ-302 | Grant LWB-115 Water Bath | 22 Apr 2025 |
| EQ-210 | Digi-Sense Thermocouple Thermometer Type K | 30 Jan 2026 |
| EQ-087 | Megger MIT525 Insulation Tester | 11 Nov 2025 |
| EQ-144 | Time/Count Data Logger, DataTaker DT85 | 08 Sep 2025 |

All equipment used was within calibration and verified against traceable standards prior to commencement.

4. TEST RESULTS SUMMARY

| Test | Requirement | Result | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4.1 | Leakage current (normal operation) | 0.12 mA | Pass |
| 4.2 | Leakage current (heating element disconnected) | 0.05 mA | Pass |
| 4.3 | Insulation resistance (cold, 500 V DC) | >99.9 MΩ | Pass |
| 4.4 | Earth continuity | 0.08 Ω | Pass |
| 4.5 | Heating time (1 L, 20°C to boiling) | 4 min 12 s | Pass |
| 4.6 | Energy consumption (1 L boil) | 0.141 kWh | Pass |
| 4.7 | Boil-dry protection activation time | 18 s | Pass |
| 4.8 | Temperature rise – handle (max) | 41 K | Pass |
| 4.9 | Temperature rise – external surface (max) | 52 K | Pass |
| 4.10 | Cord anchorage (100 N pull, 25 cycles) | No displacement | Pass |
| 4.11 | Lid stability (2x force application) | No leakage | Pass |
| 4.12 | Marking durability (rubbing test) | Legible after test | Pass |

Overall Result: PASSED

The Melbourne Testing Laboratory report shows that the test_result_pass is passed. Record status: current.

5. DETAILED OBSERVATIONS – PERFORMANCE

5.1 Heating Time (Test 4.5)

Test performed with 1.0 L of tap water at initial temperature 20.5°C, ambient 22°C. Water was heated at rated voltage 230 V. Time to reach rolling boil (100°C observed at the thermocouple positioned 20 mm above the element) was recorded as 4 min 12 s. This is within the client’s internal specification of ≤4 min 30 s.

5.2 Energy Consumption (Test 4.6)

Using the Hioki 3334, the energy consumed to bring 1.0 L from 20°C to boiling was measured at 0.141 kWh. Repeat measurement on the second sample gave 0.139 kWh. The average of 0.140 kWh is below the client’s target of 0.150 kWh.

5.3 Boil-Dry Protection (Test 4.7)

The kettle was allowed to operate with a minimal amount of water (50 mL). The element de-energised after 18 s of dry operation. The thermal cut-out reset automatically after a cooldown period of 3 min. No visible damage to the element or body was noted.

6. SAFETY TEST DETAILS

6.1 Leakage Current (Tests 4.1, 4.2)

Leakage current was measured using the circuit of Fig. 1 of AS/NZS 60335.1, with the appliance at rated voltage. In normal operation, leakage current was 0.12 mA, well below the limit of 0.75 mA for Class I appliances. With the heating element disconnected (simulated single-fault condition), the measured value was 0.05 mA, also below the limit.
